claims.text: ML-trained interatomic potentials paired with free-energy perturbation can accurately determine melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach can match traditional thermodynamic integration within acceptable error margins.
The proposed approach notably reduces computational cost relative to traditional thermodynamic integration.
Standard empirical liquid-phase EAM potentials are the initial modeling approach.
The intervention replaces empirical EAM potentials with ML-trained interatomic potentials.
The intervention replaces thermodynamic integration with free-energy perturbation.
The ML potential provides a refined representation of the free-energy landscape.
A refined free-energy landscape improves computed structural and thermodynamic properties across the melting transition.
ML-trained potentials capture complex atomic interactions in disordered high-entropy-alloy liquids better than empirical EAM potentials.
Free-energy perturbation directly computes the thermodynamic derivatives needed to determine phase-transition properties.
The combination of improved interaction modeling and free-energy perturbation enables more accurate and efficient determination of phase-transition properties than the traditional approach.
Predicted melting properties will agree with traditional thermodynamic-integration results within approximately 5–10%.
The proposed approach will reduce computational time by approximately 30–50%.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy-alloy compositions for which the ML potential has been adequately trained.
Performance outside the ML potential's training domain or under extreme conditions is uncertain.
Accuracy and efficiency gains depend on the quality and range of the ML training data.
Failure of the ML potential to capture relevant liquid-phase physics can cause deviations from the predicted performance.
